memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Go, assemble the elders of Israel and say to them, 'The Lord, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob—appeared to me and said: I have watched over you and have seen what has been done to you in Egypt. And I have promised to bring you up out of your misery in Egypt into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites—a land flowing with milk and honey.'" - Exodus 3:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives Moses a message to carry back to the elders, and at its heart is a beautiful phrase: I have watched over you.

For four centuries no prophet spoke. No miracles were recorded. From ground level it looked like heaven had gone quiet. But God says He was watching the whole time.

We should be careful how we apply this. The promise of a specific land was made to Israel under a specific covenant; it is not a guarantee that God will give us the house, job, or country we are hoping for. God's word here is not a template for our wishes.

What does carry across is God's unchanging character. He watches. He sees what is done to His people. He acts on His promises in His time.

And the deeper rescue this points to is ours in Christ. Israel was brought out of Egypt into a land; we have been brought out of the kingdom of darkness into the kingdom of God's Son (Col 1:13). That is a rescue no one can reverse.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust that God is watching even in a long silent season?
2. Have I confused God's promises with my own preferences?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You are watching over me even when I hear nothing. Thank You most of all for rescuing me through Christ. Amen.
